source.title: SharedSAE: One Feature Dictionary Across Language Models
source.authors: D. Ognev; Célian Vasson; Li-Jie Hu; Kentaro Inui; Benjamin Heinzerling

page_placements.theme: SAE dictionaries are only partly reproducible and depend on feature quality

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representational alignment using shared sparse features, code correlations, reconstruction and semantic-transfer measures rather than the original claim’s distance-geometry measures. It does not sweep model scale.
record.gate_note: The paper trains a shared dictionary, so shared latent indices are encouraged by the method; results bearing on convergence are the reported solo-selection, magnitude, semantic-transfer, reconstruction and cross-corpus measurements, not the forced index sharing by itself. Omitted descriptions of prior work are cited results, not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: A method paper that trains one shared SAE dictionary across four ~1B base LMs (Qwen3, Llama-3.2, OLMo-2, Gemma-3). Much of the measured sharedness is encouraged by the objective (shared dictionary, cross-reconstruction loss, vote-source dropout). Some results still bear on V4 and V5: how well one shared sparse code reconstructs and cross-maps each model, a raw-stream ridge map, adaptation of held-out, hybrid, instruct and cross-lab models, and post-hoc matching of independently trained per-model SAEs. Functional agreement and Wikipedia re-evaluation bear weakly on V6 and V7. No scale sweep, no vision models, and no LM seed comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a shared sparse dictionary can be learned for their four-model roster. It reconstructs each model near dedicated quality, its latents are chosen consistently, correlate in magnitude and carry transferable meanings, and new models can be attached to the frozen dictionary. They call functional alignment partial. They treat the Platonic hypothesis as background, not a premise, and claim only the narrower result for this roster. They also state sharedness survives a corpus the SAE never saw.
record.recipe_differences: The study jointly trains a shared sparse dictionary and model-specific encoder-decoder pairs, then measures alignment and adaptation; it does not use the original representation-distance geometry method or test convergence with scale.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with joint versus solo TopK selection and with hook depth. The paper reports broadly similar sharedness on Wikipedia but lower listed values than the main FineWeb-Edu measurements; it also notes dependence on aligned-data amount, training budget and SAE settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Two SAEs trained from different seeds on Qwen3-1.7B activations match at 0.770 best-match and 0.871 mutual-best activation correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries trained from different seeds on the same model's activations recover largely overlapping but non-identical features.

record.problems: The roster is four base checkpoints around 1B parameters, trained on English FineWeb-Edu; there is no scale sweep or performance comparison. The shared dictionary is jointly optimized to align latents, and two sharedness criteria are affected by training pressure. The semantic evaluation filters on clarity, functional alignment is partial, several metrics are proxies, and some appendices use an earlier protocol. The seed comparison is one seed pair on one stream.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version result rows retained beyond the listed results. Omitted detailed per-category FADE entries, ablations of SAE components, qualitative examples, and unrelated reconstruction diagnostics; they do not add a distinct claim-relevant model/condition result beyond the aggregate measures recorded here.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; all models are about 1–2B.
No LMs trained from different initializations. Only SAE-seed stability on one LM is reported.
Unpaired mapping, relative representations and model stitching are not tested.
Similarity-measure settings (e.g. neighbours), other languages and broad distribution shifts beyond one Wikipedia store.
Whether shared pretraining data or objectives explain alignment; plateau with scale.

missing.what: Matched dedicated (independently trained) SAE control as its own results: top-50 overlap 13.5/50 (300k) and pairwise 15 (11–17) on 100k; modal-token agreement 0.45; token Jaccard 0.19; AP retention 0.973. These are the natural, non-induced universality evidence.
No-dictionary floor: matching raw residual dimensions across models by best correlation gives median |r| 0.14.
missing.locator: Appendix D.4, Floor without a dictionary

missing.what: Cross-model code splice: one model's code decoded by another recovers 0.92–0.96 of the CE gap (mean 0.94) vs 0.95–0.97 for own code; KL roughly doubles.
missing.locator: Appendix D.4, Decoding one model's code into another

missing.what: Linear (Atlas-style ridge) attach into a seed stream: FVE share 0.692 (Gemma fold) and 0.670 (Qwen3.5) vs 0.984 and 0.972 for the adapted encoder-decoder.
Weight-space agreement, which does not depend on TopK: decoder SVCCA 0.34 vs 0.17 shuffled floor; latent RSA 0.31 vs 0.00. Weaker than selection-based measures.
missing.locator: Appendix D.4, Agreement in the weights

missing.what: SPARC per-latent correlation is 0.937 under joint TopK but 0.000 solo, driven by a usage-breadth population effect. An example of metric and population dependence.
Only 24 latents (0.07% of the dictionary) respond in one model alone under a raw-encoder probe without TopK.
Cross-model steering: same latent shifts every model toward the same concept (lift 0.16–0.22 at alpha=1); token-level detectors never steer.

record.verdict_notes: Sharedness in SharedSAE is partly built in by the objective, so its own rows are weaker evidence than natural comparators. The post-hoc matched control and raw ridge map are the cleanest non-induced evidence and should be rows. The Wikipedia check concerns the SAE's training corpus, not the LMs' pretraining data, so it does not bear on V7's shared-data explanation. The reader's V7 'challenges' label was removed for this reason. Baselines for R23, R24 and R25 were wrong and are corrected above.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no test of whether alignment rises with scale.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
Only one reported same-model seed-pair comparison; this does not establish feature convergence across a broad seed or architecture sample.

Tests a jointly trained shared sparse dictionary with model-specific encoders and decoders, including held-out adaptation. Does not test unpaired mapping or whether a simple linear map or stitching alone suffices.
Tests shared SAE latents and descriptions across language models, not recurrence of particular neurons or circuits independently discovered in each model.

Tests several alignment measures and selection conditions, a Wikipedia evaluation corpus, and a mid-depth setting. Does not establish dependence across broad data distributions, languages, metric settings, or out-of-distribution model families.

Reports incomplete functional alignment and tests whether the result is specific to the shared training corpus. Does not isolate the effects of shared model objectives or establish a common model of reality.

rows.check: Joint TopK makes all models co-fire by construction; the authors say this partly measures selection, not representation.

rows.check: Solo agreement is still encouraged by vote-source dropout and the cross loss, so it is partly by construction. Natural comparator is the post-hoc matched control (median 0.428, 35% above 0.5).
